stories.summary: Andy Jurgis writes: Douglas Dunn was delighted to hear about the visit to Hirta In the early 1980s I heard a poetry reading by Douglas Dunn in the Morden Tower, Newcastle upon Tyne. After that I kept up to date with his new work. Many years later I discussed his well-known poem St Kilda’s Parliament with my students at an adult education class in Frodsham, Cheshire. One was so enthused that she undertook an adventurous visit to Hirta , the main island of the St Kilda archipelago in the Outer Hebrides. Douglas was delighted to hear about the trip at a reading at Manchester University that focused on his last collection, The Noise of a Fly (2017).
